[b]Barrier X will have you staring into strobe lights as they light your face and eyes with a boatload of colour, all the while your brain is attempting to comprehend the mechanics of the game as you zip, zap & attack across an inconceivable path.[/b]

The steam description does not lie, the game is fast and throws challenging mechanics at you with each new level; for example one stage will introduce near mandatory lanes that punish you if missed while another stage will introduce an AI combatant that you're required to destroy before it kills you. The mechanics can be mastered and beaten but the amount of visual clutter is overwhelming, regardless if you get into a flow state the game is incredibly addicting.

Barrier X is chaotic & not for those prone to sensory overload, It riddles you with effects & distorts time when you’re in a flow state; seconds feel like less and it’s easy to lose a chunk of time trying to improve your records. If you're into high speed endless runners or rhythm games you'll more than likely enjoy Barrier X & its challenges but if you want a chill runner, I don’t think it’s for you.

If you do end up purchasing & playing the title, I recommend your own music playlist over the in-game soundtrack. I found [i]Bury the Light by Casey Edwards & Victor Borba[/i] and [i]Cult of Personality by Living Colour[/i] fit the gameplay flow perfectly. 

[i]Personal note:[/i] I was curious to see how I reacted to the stimulation and quick thinking the game oozes, so I recorded a five minute run where I died & beat my record numerous times; It was fascinating watching my pupils dilate, face flash with various colours and my microsecond reaction before starting another run after swift failure.

[b]Barrier X if it meets your criteria is worth $4.50AUD but if you aren't quite sure I recommend picking up the game when it drops to $1.35 during sales.[/b]

I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

I couldn't decide whether to recommend this or not until I gave it some more effort. The game is fun for the first three levels and is a cool idea, but it just goes downhill from there. As someone in the target audience, this doesn't really meet the mark of other similar games.

The visuals are obnoxious, and often times the things you need to hit are either blocking or being blocked by something you need to avoid, resulting in some borderline unwinnable conditions. The constant slowdown and speedup leads to many dropped inputs, which is especially a detriment in a game like this. Additionally, the constant mashing required because the game doesn't have auto fire is atrocious. A lot of games don't need auto fire, but this one does. The shooting aspect doesn't really add much to the game either. I think this could be a solid game if it just focused on the mechanics of the first 3 stages, and toned down the visuals a bit. As someone who enjoyed a game called AVOID SENSORY OVERLOAD, that's saying something...

Un titulo en el que hasta la pantalla de juego aparece como un accidente de trafico sabe lo que esta haciendo.
BARRIER X es de esos videojuegos brillantemente simples, brutalmente adictivos y con un diseño perfectamente medido, algo así como super hexagon en una autopista a la velocidad del sonido.

Pero acá esta el toque distintivo, super hexagon subía la dificultad haciendo que sus paredes fuesen mas deprisa y con nuevos patrones pensados para joderte la vida pero BARRIER X añade nuevas capas al desafió.
Primero tienes que esquivar, luego esquivar para determinada dirección, luego hay ciertos muros que tenes que estamparte pero puedes saltarte estas indicaciones si pulsas un botón a tiempo así que el resultado parece mucho mas agitado.
No solo te estas moviendo de izquierda a derecha sino realizando cálculos sobre que indicaciones ignorar, cuales realizar, que muros vienen a continuación y como el juego pasa de 0 a 100 en un instante y cada 15 segundos acelera un poco mas, es una serie de intensivos constantes que transmiten ese no parar. Como cada vez te mueves de forma mas arriesgada.
BARRIER X parece haber destilado la formula de la velocidad y esta enamorado del impulso, de la esquiva en el ultimo segundo, de las carreras a fuego y ese constante impacto, es pura sensación de velocidad.

Sera pequeño y sencillo pero explota como una bomba, es intenso y aunque no sea mas desafiante que super hexagon, te hace sentir como un campeón.
